Convergence 01

A pure function of progress — no accumulated state — so seeking backwards lands on exactly the frame it left.

Cloud 02

Resamples the mesh on release. Every splat costs a kNN fit once and a sort key forever — the honest trade in this technique.

Cutoff is where the Gaussian's quad stops. Below ~2σ the discs get visibly clipped; above ~3σ you pay fill rate for e^-4.5 of alpha.

Backdrop 03

A splat carries its own baked colour and reflects nothing, so there is no room to build — only something for its accumulated edges to sit against.

Camera 04

Drag steers in any mode and decays back to the move.

Method A mesh resampled into Gaussians, not a capture. Points are placed by area-weighted barycentric sampling so coverage follows surface rather than triangle count, coloured from the model's real baked albedo, and each one is fitted a covariance from its own neighbours — flattened along the normal, stretched in the tangent plane. They are rasterised by EWA splatting: the 3D covariance pushed through the projection's Jacobian into a screen-space conic, evaluated as a true Gaussian, blended back to front. The training run is the one invented part, and it is invented so it can be scrubbed.
